technique_why: A sunset landscape with one big shaggy animal in front is the classic back-to-front paint-along: sky, mountains and hills go on in big easy shapes, and the cow's coat builds from flat shape to long locks in plain repeated strokes.
subject: A shaggy Highland cow standing in a tall golden-green meadow at sunset, with rolling green hills, blue mountains and a glimpse of a lake behind it
focal_point: The cow's head: the fringe falling over its eyes, the pink nose and the two curving horns
light: A low setting sun at the right, just above the far mountains, lighting the cow from behind and to the right so the top of its head, its fringe and its right side glow gold
why: The sky, clouds, mountains and hills go on first as big, quick shapes that a beginner can't really get wrong, so most of the time goes to the cow. The cow is built like a teacher would: a flat rust shape, its shadows, the horns, then locks of hair in lighter passes. The meadow grass is flicked over the cow's legs afterwards, and the sunlit rim and the face come last, so the lesson ends on the part the eye goes to.

things.name: The sunset sky
things.why: A smooth blue-to-gold sunset blended wet in one go, run down past the mountains.

things.name: The sunset clouds
things.why: Soft streaks of peach and rose with gold tops, dry-brushed onto the dry sky.
things.plain: soft peach and dusky rose cloud streaks with no gold tops

things.name: The far blue mountains
things.why: Two ranges of distant mountains with no texture, the far one paler and more violet.
things.plain: flat blue-violet mountain ranges with no warm light on the ridges

things.name: The glimpse of lake
things.why: A thin pale strip of water at the far right where the hills dip, laid in with level strokes; it is too small to need ripples.

things.name: The rolling green hills
things.why: The green slopes behind the cow are a field seen from a distance: a base, then darker bands along the slopes, no texture.
things.plain: smooth light-green slopes with no darker bands or bushes

things.name: The dark bushes on the hills
things.why: Small far bushes and shrubs dotted over the slopes; only the dark dab, since far trees get no detail.

things.name: The tall meadow grass
things.why: The foreground grass the cow stands in: a green base, then slanted grass marks flicked over it in three passes, dark to gold, over the cow's legs.
things.plain: a smooth green meadow with a darker front and no grass marks

things.name: The Highland cow
things.why: A long-haired cow whose coat hangs in locks over a darker body, lit from behind, with its eyes under a fringe: exactly this element.
things.plain: the plain flat rust-brown cow shape
things.left_out: Single hairs, fine wisps at the coat's edge, and the eyes, which stay hidden under the fringe as in the finish.

things.name: The cow's horns
things.why: Two curved horns with a pale lit side and darker tips, built as tapering curved shapes, then shaded and lit.
things.plain: two flat pale tan horn shapes with no shading

paints.name: Hill green

paints.name: Yellow green

steps.name: Blend the sunset sky

lays.what: the whole sky from the top edge down to about the middle of the canvas: blue at the top, fading through pale cream to gold at the horizon, brightest gold low on the right where the sun sets

steps.after: The top half of the canvas is a smooth sky, blue at the top, creamy in the middle and gold near the middle of the canvas, brightest at the right. There are no clouds yet, and everything below is bare white canvas.
steps.why: The sky is farthest away, and it runs past where the mountains and hills will go so its strokes stay long.

steps.name: Dry-brush the cloud streaks

lays.what: long, slanted soft cloud streaks across the upper sky, peach on top and dusky rose along their undersides, smaller and thinner toward the horizon

steps.after: Soft, broken streaks of peach and dusky rose lie across the upper sky, with the blue showing through their edges. They have no gold tops yet. Below the sky the canvas is still white.

steps.name: Light the tops of the clouds

lays.what: golden yellow on the upper edges of the cloud streaks, more on the clouds nearest the sun at right

steps.after: The cloud streaks have glowing gold tops over their peach and rose, the rose still showing underneath. Below the sky the canvas is still white.

stages.name: The far mountains and the lake

steps.name: Lay in the far mountains

lays.what: the far range as a pale blue-violet band of soft peaks across the canvas, then the nearer, darker slate-blue ridges overlapping its foot, lowest and darkest just above where the hills will start

steps.after: Two flat ranges of mountains cross the canvas just below the gold horizon, pale violet behind and slate blue in front, with no warm light on them. Below them the canvas is bare white.
steps.why: The mountains go on over the dry sky, farthest range first.

steps.name: Catch the sunset on the ridges

lays.what: a thin warm peach glow skimmed along the tops of the ridges facing the sun, mostly on the right

steps.after: The mountain ridges have a faint warm peach edge on the sun side; the rest of each range stays its flat blue. Below them the canvas is bare white.

steps.name: Lay in the strip of lake

lays.what: a thin pale cream strip of water at the far right, at the foot of the mountains

steps.after: A short, thin, pale strip of lake shines at the right edge at the foot of the mountains. Below it the canvas is bare white.

steps.name: Lay in the hills and meadow

lays.what: the rolling slopes from the foot of the mountains down to about two-thirds of the way down the canvas, sloping down to the right, lighter yellow-green at the back
the whole bottom of the canvas below the hills down to the bottom edge, in the same greens, a little darker toward the bottom

steps.after: Everything below the mountains is a smooth green base, lighter yellow-green on the far slopes and olive green lower down. There are no bands, bushes or grass marks yet, and no cow.
steps.why: One base for all the green ground, with the brush already loaded: the hills and the meadow are the same greens, lighter at the back.

steps.name: Darken the hill bands and meadow front

lays.what: darker blue-green bands along the slopes, following their roll, with the light green left between them
a darker blue-green over the lower part of the meadow toward the bottom edge

steps.after: The hills now have alternating dark and light green bands, and the meadow darkens toward the bottom of the canvas. There are no bushes or grass marks yet, and no cow.
steps.why: The same dark green and the same level strokes do both: it is one pass of the darker green over the ground.

steps.name: Dab the dark bushes on the hills

lays.what: small round clumps of dark blue-green bushes dotted over the hills, smaller and paler toward the back

steps.after: Small dark round bushes dot the green hills. The meadow is a plain green base with no grass marks, and there is no cow yet.

steps.name: Block in the cow

lays.what: the whole cow as one flat rust-brown shape on the left of center: a big upright oval for the shaggy body, a rounded head on its right with the fringe as a curved cap over it, and the lower body fading into the meadow, every stroke curving down the way the hair hangs

steps.after: A flat rust-brown cow shape stands in the meadow, head to the right of its body. It has no shadows, no locks, no horns and no face.
steps.why: Ugly-stage point: a flat brown blob is exactly right here.

steps.name: Shade the side away from the light

lays.what: deep brown in long downward curves on the left side of the body, under the fringe and chin, in the gaps where the locks will part, and low on the body

steps.after: The rust cow has deep brown shadows down its left side, under its fringe and chin, and low on its body; the right side is still plain rust. It has no locks, horns or face.

steps.name: Block in the horns

lays.what: two long curving horns from either side of the top of the head: each a wide piece at the head, then a curving piece that tapers to a point, the left one rising high and the right one curving up

steps.after: Two flat pale tan horns curve up from the cow's head with no shading or dark tips. The coat is still rust and dark brown with no locks.
steps.why: The horns go on before the locks, so the fringe can fall over their bases.

steps.name: Shade the horns and their tips

lays.what: dark brown on the undersides of both horns and at their tips, blending out along the curve

steps.after: The horns have dark brown tips and undersides with the pale tan along their tops. The coat is still rust and dark brown with no locks.

steps.name: Pull the ginger locks

lays.what: long ginger-orange locks hanging down over the body, head and fringe, each wide at the top and tapering to a point, following the body's curve, with dark brown showing between them, fewer on the left

steps.after: The cow's coat is long ginger locks over rust, with dark brown gaps between them; the fringe hangs over the eyes in locks. There are no gold locks or glowing rim yet, and the nose is still plain coat color.

steps.name: Pull the honey-gold locks

lays.what: fewer, smaller honey-gold locks over the ginger ones, mostly on the fringe, the top of the head and the right side of the body

steps.after: Honey-gold locks lie over the ginger ones on the fringe, head and right side, with ginger and dark brown still showing. There is no bright glowing rim yet and no nose.

steps.name: Flick the dark grass

lays.what: slanted dark blue-green grass marks over the whole meadow and over the cow's legs and lower body, bigger toward the bottom

steps.after: Dark slanted grass marks cover the meadow and hide the cow's legs and lower body. There are no light green or gold grass marks yet.
steps.why: The grass in front of the cow goes on after the cow, over it.

steps.name: Flick the yellow-green grass

lays.what: slanted yellow-green grass marks between the dark ones across the meadow and over the cow's lower edge, fewer toward the hills

steps.after: The meadow is a mix of dark and yellow-green slanted marks, with the dark showing between them. There are no gold grass marks yet.

steps.name: Flick the golden grass

lays.what: a scatter of honey-gold slanted grass marks across the meadow, most around the cow and at the bottom left

steps.after: The meadow is full: dark, yellow-green and golden slanted grass marks, with the dark still showing between them. The cow has no glowing rim and no nose yet.

steps.name: Light the rim of the coat

lays.what: short bright gold tapering strokes on the edges facing the sun: the top of the head, the fringe, the right edge of the head and chest, and the top of the back

steps.after: The cow's head, fringe and right side glow with a bright gold rim, much smaller than the locks under it. The horns have no light along their tops yet, and the cow has no nose.

steps.name: Light the tops of the horns

lays.what: pale cream along the upper, sunlit edge of each horn

steps.after: The horns have a pale cream light along their tops over the tan, with the dark tips and undersides still showing. The cow has no nose yet.

steps.name: Paint the nose

lays.what: the broad rounded nose and muzzle under the fringe, right of center on the head, in a muted pinkish brown

steps.after: A flat pinkish-brown rounded nose sits under the fringe, with no highlight, nostrils or mouth.

steps.name: Light the top of the nose

lays.what: pale pink on the top of the nose, between where the nostrils will go

steps.after: The nose has a pale pink top over the pinkish brown. It has no nostrils or mouth yet.

steps.name: Line the nostrils and mouth

lays.what: two short dark curved nostrils on either side of the nose and a short dark mouth line below it

steps.after: The finished painting: the cow has dark nostrils and a mouth line under its pink nose, under a glowing fringe, in a golden meadow below the sunset.
